Example Itineraries / Sailing Voyages

10-Day Sailing Expedition

Luna Moon
Nosy Be to Mahajanga

10 days
115-year-old historic schooner
Northwest Madagascar coastline
Best: May – November
“This is not just a voyage — it is an immersive exploration of remote islands, vibrant marine life and some of the most pristine anchorages in the Indian Ocean.”

Luna Moon is a magnificent 132ft historic top-sail gaff-rigged schooner — the only fully operational vessel of her kind in the Indian Ocean. Built 115 years ago, she carries up to 8 guests in private cabins, with spacious decks, a dedicated crew and freshly prepared meals inspired by local seafood and seasonal produce.

From the lush shores of Nosy Be to the cultural richness of Mahajanga, this expedition blends adventure, relaxation and authentic discovery in true barefoot luxury.

Days 1–2
Islands
Days 1–2
Nosy Be

Embarkation & The Archipelago

Step aboard Luna Moon in Nosy Be — the Perfume Island — and feel the rhythm of the Indian Ocean beneath you from the very first moment. Before setting sail, spend time exploring the islands closest to home: Nosy Tanikely with its spectacular protected reef, the calm turtle sanctuary bays of Sakatia, and Nosy Komba's sacred black lemur forest and vibrant beach market. These early days set the tone perfectly — unhurried, immersive and full of discovery. As the sun goes down on your first evening aboard, the crew serve sundowners on the deck while the Nosy Be archipelago glows in the fading light.

Board Luna Moon in Nosy Be harbourNosy Tanikely snorkellingNosy Sakatia sea turtlesNosy Komba lemurs & beach marketFirst sunset at anchor
Luna Moon accommodates up to 8 guests in private cabins. All meals are prepared fresh on board by the ship's cook, inspired by local seafood and seasonal produce.
Day 3
Marine
Day 3
Russian Bay & Nosy Iranja

Legend & the Iconic Sandbar

Sail south along the coast to Russian Bay — Ambavatory Bay — a captivating and atmospheric inlet steeped in maritime legend. The bay takes its name from an event around 1905, during the Russo-Japanese War, when a Russian warship reportedly anchored here and whose crew chose not to return home. Remnants of this extraordinary story — including rumoured graves and traces of the vessel — are still associated with the bay today. From Russian Bay, continue to Nosy Iranja, Madagascar's most iconic destination: two small islands connected at low tide by a dazzling white sandbar stretching into turquoise water. Anchor offshore and spend the afternoon swimming and exploring before a seafood dinner as the stars emerge.

Anchor in atmospheric Russian BayMaritime legend of the 1905 Russian warshipNosy Iranja iconic twin-island sandbarSwimming & snorkelling in the lagoonSunset dinner at anchor
Nosy Iranja's sandbar is at its most dramatic at low tide — the crew plan the visit around tidal timings for maximum effect.
Days 4–5
Marine
Days 4–5
Radama Islands

The Pristine Radama Archipelago

Sail to the Radama Islands — a pristine archipelago of four idyllic islands named in honour of King Radama I, who was crowned at just 17 years old in 1810 and became the first ruler to unify much of Madagascar. Today the Radamas are celebrated for their extraordinary marine biodiversity: pristine beaches, crystal-clear water and vibrant coral reefs that provide some of the finest snorkelling and diving in the Indian Ocean. The remote location means very few other visitors — the islands feel entirely your own. Sport fishing opportunities here are exceptional, and the crew are happy to organise lines and tackle.

Named after King Radama I — Madagascar's unifierPristine coral reefs & exceptional snorkellingWorld-class sport fishingRemote anchorages — few other visitorsSwimming from the boat in crystal-clear water
The Radama Islands offer some of the most secluded anchorages on the entire voyage. Fresh fish caught by the crew may well feature on the evening menu.
Day 6
Adventure
Day 6
Nosy Lava

History & Hidden Wilderness

A hidden gem with fascinating history and raw natural beauty. Nosy Lava is a remote island south of the Radamas that served as a maximum-security French colonial penal colony until 2002, when several prisoners escaped and the facility was disbanded. Visitors can still explore the remains of the historic prison that once housed political detainees alongside ordinary prisoners — an eerie and thought-provoking stop that adds real depth to the voyage. Beyond its history, Nosy Lava offers towering limestone cliffs, coconut palms and white sand beaches of extraordinary beauty.

Explore the abandoned colonial penal colonyPrison ruins dating to the French colonial eraTowering limestone cliffs & white sand beachesCoconut palms and remote wildernessUnique historical perspective on Madagascar's past
A guide accompanies visits to the prison ruins. The history here is significant — the crew provide context before going ashore.
Days 7–8
Adventure
Days 7–8
Baie de Moramba

A Miniature Halong Bay

One of the most extraordinary stops on the entire voyage. Baie de Moramba, located near the Anjajavy Peninsula, is a breathtaking natural wonder renowned for its maze of mushroom-shaped limestone tsingy formations rising from emerald water — often compared to a miniature Halong Bay. The area is best explored by tender or kayak, weaving between the formations to discover hidden coves, secluded beaches and mangrove forests thick with birdlife. Flocks of parrots and other endemic species inhabit the surrounding cliffs, and the sense of wilderness here is profound.

Limestone tsingy formations rising from the waterKayak through hidden coves & mangrove channelsEndemic parrots & cliff-nesting birdsDeserted beaches accessible only by boatOne of Madagascar's most dramatic natural landscapes
The bay is best explored by tender and kayak — both are carried aboard Luna Moon. Early morning provides the best light and the calmest conditions.
Days 9–10
Culture
Days 9–10
Mahajanga

Journey's End in Mahajanga

The final days of the voyage bring you to Mahajanga — also known as Majunga — a vibrant coastal town where African, Arab, Indian and French influences converge to create a cultural atmosphere unique to Madagascar's west coast. Stroll the famous promenade beneath towering baobab trees, explore the colourful markets and bustling local neighbourhoods, and watch one of the most spectacular sunsets on the entire Mozambique Channel. Before disembarkation, a visit to Katsepy — a small fishing village across the Bay of Bombetoka — reveals both authentic local life and the remarkable crowned sifaka lemurs that inhabit the surrounding area.

Mahajanga waterfront & baobab-lined promenadeMulticultural market & colonial architectureKatsepy fishing village across the bayCrowned sifaka lemur habitatFinal sunset over the Mozambique Channel
Disembarkation in Mahajanga. TMC can arrange onward flights to Antananarivo or connections to other parts of Madagascar. Ask about extending your journey.

Optional Activities

Experience More

Optional excursions and activities are available throughout the voyage.

Marine
Snorkelling at Nosy Tanikely

World-class protected reef with exceptional visibility — one of the finest snorkel sites in Madagascar.

Marine
Sakatia Sea Turtle Encounter

Snorkel alongside resident green sea turtles in the calm bays of Nosy Sakatia.

Wildlife
Nosy Komba Lemur Walk

Guided walk through protected forest where semi-wild black lemurs roam freely.

Adventure
Sport Fishing — Radama Islands

The remote Radama Islands offer exceptional sport fishing in virtually untouched waters.

Culture
Katsepy Village & Sifaka Lemurs

Cross the Bay of Bombetoka to this rustic fishing village — home to the striking crowned sifaka lemur.

Adventure
Kayaking — Baie de Moramba

Explore the extraordinary limestone tsingy formations and hidden coves by kayak.

A voyage like no other

Luna Moon carries a maximum of 8 guests, making every voyage an intimate and highly personalised experience. The route, pace and activities can be tailored around your group — whether you want more time at anchor in the Radamas, an extra day exploring Baie de Moramba, or a different start or end point entirely.

Tell us about your group and we’ll come back within 24 hours to begin designing your voyage.
